rationale: A wins because it keeps the hard parts hard: "Without the mobile-billing answer, the comparison is not apples to apples" is exactly the caveat that decides whether this pitch survives an editor. B has the same raw instincts, but it lets shakier framing through, especially "Discord's move signals monetization is coming for the whole server, not just the streamer," a category claim the supplied facts cannot carry. A tells the founder what to prove before pitching; B still has thesis filler to burn off.
gaps_in_A: "unpaid volunteer community managers" and "moderating for free" are plausible Discord-world color, but not supplied facts. Useful lens, slightly overdecorated.

"Discord takes 10% where Apple takes 30%" sharpens the fee fight, but the update only gives the 30% app-store standard. It mostly fixes this by demanding the mobile-billing answer, but the headline is still a little ahead of the proof.

The contrarian angle leans on "The prevailing belief is that a 200-million-user base plus a cheap take rate is an obvious win." A admits that is inferred, which saves it, but it still needs outside support before anyone pitches it.
gaps_in_B: "Discord undercuts Apple and Google" names specific opponents the update did not name, and "on its own turf" implies billing control that has not been proven. That is how a good fee angle gets a correction slapped on it.

"how this revenue stream fits alongside existing lines (ads, Nitro)" imports business lines not supplied in the update. Proof requests can use outside reporting, but they should not smuggle in facts as if the brief gave them to you.

"Discord's move signals monetization is coming for the whole server, not just the streamer" is the padded one. The brief says server owners can charge for premium roles and content; it does not establish a structural shift away from streamers.

"Does premium content on gaming servers include anything gambling- or loot-box-adjacent?" is a speculative detour. Interesting after evidence appears; not one of the founder's first four questions from this fact set.
